failing.summary: RELEASE.md:3; docs/how-to/install.md:242 (raised by opus): Both pages say that once ~/.abcd.noindex/.gitignore exists, the next `git add -A` skips everything abcd keeps there ('nothing private leaves the machine by accident'; 'stages nothing abcd keeps there'). That is false for a file the home repository already tracks: git applies .gitignore to untracked paths only, so `git add -A` still stages changes to an already-tracked ~/.abcd.noindex/config.json or memory.json. homeignore.Lay only writes the ignore file and marker. CHANGELOG.md:11 states the exception ('does not untrack anything your home repository already tracks'), but neither page does. A person whose dotfiles repository already tracks abcd's home reads that they are covered and keeps pushing. Fix with one clause on each page, for example: 'It does not untrack a file your home repository already tracks; to stop tracking those, run `git rm -r --cached .abcd.noindex` in your home repository.' RELEASE.md also says 'The first time abcd runs' without the status-line exception that the changelog and install.md give (nitpick).
failing.note: Fixed after the content commit in a3718a67b: both pages now say the ignore file leaves a file the home repository already tracks tracked. An Opus and Sonnet pair confirmed the fix (the Opus agent against real git), both PROMOTE.

failing.summary: CHANGELOG.md:16; RELEASE.md:7 (raised by opus): The entry says that with `oracle.review = rp` in the repository's or the machine's configuration, a build lane sends its reviews to RepoPrompt.
